page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v6 is a low-memory, local-disk variant within Azure's general-purpose virtual machine lineup, provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. The compute configuration provides 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. Architectural instruction support is extensive, featuring AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions with AMX Tile and AMX INT8). Memory is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio (2.0 GB per core). For high-speed temporary storage, the instance bundles a dedicated 236 GB NVMe SSD. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included.

Benchmark evaluation displays a mix of strong single-threaded performance coupled with lower throughput in memory-bound and multi-core tasks. The Intel Xeon 8573C demonstrates upper-quartile performance in Geekbench single-core (2141.0), single-threaded gzip compression (31.32 GB/sec), and Geekbench text processing (2535.0). Multi-threaded compute results place closer to median thresholds, recording 4805.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 7398.11 on PassMark CPU score. However, stress-ng multi-core (3990.56) and memory subsystem benchmarks—including PassMark memory (1693.71), read-only large-block bandwidth (36.76 GB/sec), and large-block write bandwidth (25.84 GB/sec)—fall into the lowest 25% bracket.

Cost efficiency is focused around workloads requiring dedicated per-vCPU throughput and fast local disk scratch space without the overhead of excess memory. The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio limits its viability for large in-memory databases, as shown by Redis SET performance ranking in the bottom quartile (5.69 million ops/sec). The instance is well-suited for web frontends, lightweight batch processing, single-threaded application servers, CI/CD runners, and edge inference on small models that fit comfortably within the 8.0 GB RAM envelope.
description: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v6 is a compute-leaning, low-memory virtual machine powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD for fast local temporary storage, without GPU accelerators. The CPU features Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector support, translating to strong single-core benchmarks, notably in Geekbench single-core (2141.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (31.32 GB/sec). However, multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth tests fall into lower percentiles due to core count constraints and memory architecture limits. With a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, the D4lds_v6 is most effective for web serving, build pipelines, and processing pipelines needing local NVMe scratch storage rather than large memory footprints.
